review_note: Reviewer 2, 2026-11-02. Test builds A (AR(1) correlation times a non-unit scale, shuffled) itself and evaluates a base-R dense Laplace oracle for animal(1|animal_id, A) + (1|site) with separate SD regressions, at the fitted parameters of BOTH the native and the Julia fit (rel. tol 2e-4, i.e. about 0.5 absolute at logLik -2562); native-vs-Julia parity is additional, not the oracle. The one linked row (Julia, binomial, logit, iid + animal A_covariance) is exercised by fit_julia with A. Sensitivity demonstrated in a scratch run on Totoro (native fit, test oracle function, no files edited): oracle-minus-logLik 8e-12; swapped selector coefficient sets shifts the oracle by 61.0; sign-flipped animal predictor 0.96; reversed animal SD vector 0.96; A*2 2.34; cov2cor(A) 0.80. Only swapped selectors is far beyond tolerance; the other perturbations are 1.6-4.6 times the 0.5 absolute tolerance. Rerun 39 pass/0 fail/0 skip, console shows 1 live Julia test ran. Manifest (5 files): 4 match; R/julia-bridge.R differs at HEAD from e9c72ab3e (the change only adds the NB2 spatial-slope route, no Binomial path), so the rerun at e9c72ab3e is the evidence. Does NOT establish: calibration or coverage; Julia accuracy beyond this fixture at tolerance 2e-4 relative; probit/cloglog; slope or non-iid structured providers; the Ainv path against an oracle (Ainv is compared only with A); the 'sd_animal' SD regression behaviour on any other kernel; that smaller kernel/SD mistakes below about 0.5 logLik units would be caught.
